claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
## Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Summary:**
You meet all the requirements to claim Child Benefit for Alex. The key factors are:

✅ **Alex is 15 years old** - under the age limit of 16  
✅ **You live in the UK** - meeting the residence requirement  
✅ **Alex lives with you** - establishing your responsibility  
✅ **Fostering situation is acceptable** - Crucially, because the local council is NOT paying for Alex's accommodation or maintenance, you qualify for Child Benefit. The government rules specifically allow foster carers to claim Child Benefit in this situation.  
✅ **No disqualifying factors** - Alex is not in care, doesn't work 24+ hours/week, hasn't started an apprenticeship, and doesn't receive benefits in their own right

**What to do next:**
You can apply for Child Benefit through the government website or by contacting the Child Benefit Office.

**Note:** If you or your partner earn over £60,000 per year individually, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit Tax Charge, but you can still claim the benefit.

reasonings:
According to the official eligibility criteria, you qualify for Child Benefit for Alex based on the following:

1. Age requirement: Alex is 15 years old, which is under the age limit of 16 for automatic qualification.

2. Residence: You live in the UK, which meets the residence requirement.

3. Responsibility for the child: Alex lives with you, which establishes that you are responsible for them.

4. Care status: Alex is not in local authority care, so there are no care-related restrictions on your eligibility.

5. Hospital/residential accommodation: Alex is not in hospital or residential accommodation, so the 12-week rule does not apply.

6. Fostering situation: Although Alex is fostered, the government guidance specifically states 'You'll get Child Benefit if you foster a child, as long as the local council is not paying anything towards their accommodation or maintenance.' Since the council is not paying for Alex's accommodation or maintenance, you qualify for Child Benefit.

7. Work status: Alex does not work 24+ hours per week, so there's no disqualification on those grounds.

8. Apprenticeship: Alex has not started an apprenticeship in England.

9. Benefits: Alex does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance), which would disqualify them.

All eligibility criteria are met for Alex.
